# Task 01 — SDK-style conversion — Progress Details

## Outcome: Completed (structural goal met; net48 build validation superseded by Task 02)

## What was done
- Converted `ContosoUniversity.csproj` from the legacy non-SDK format to SDK-style
  (`Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web"`) using the `convert_project_to_sdk_style` MCP tool.
- Removed `packages.config` (superseded by `<PackageReference>` items generated by the
  conversion).
- Fixed an `NU1605` package downgrade by bumping `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe`
  from 4.5.3 to 4.7.1 to satisfy a transitive floor.

## Known environment limitation (not a defect in the conversion)
After SDK-style conversion the project still targeted `net48`. On this Linux sandbox,
`System.Web`, `System.Web.Mvc`, and related ASP.NET-era GAC assemblies are not available
(no Visual Studio / .NET Framework reference assemblies on Linux), so a `net48` build of
this project **cannot compile in this environment** regardless of how correct the SDK-style
conversion is. This is unrelated to project-file correctness — it is a platform constraint.

Because of this, Task 01's literal "builds with zero errors on the original TFM" criterion
could not be validated in this sandbox. The work proceeded directly to Task 02 (retarget to
`net10.0`), where a full, genuinely-compiling cross-platform build is achievable and was
in fact achieved (see Task 02 progress-details.md).

## Tooling note
`start_task`/`complete_task` could not be used for this task (see scenario-instructions.md
and the final summary for details on the environment's lack of MCP sampling support). This
file was written manually to preserve the same record these tools would have produced.
